why: Tier-1 tooling: one new module scripts/ops/predicted_register_integrity.py, an optional no-op-when-unused hook on scripts/ops/github_equivalent_merge.py, one new check in scripts/ops/manager_preflight.py, one new test file, and one CORRECTED row in docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json. No src/, no config/, no deploy/, no workflows. NOT in LANDING_MACHINERY (verified against the tuple, which names claude-pr-automerge.yml, pr-opener.yml and board-post.yml), so R12 does not apply. WHAT IT FIXES: github_equivalent_merge.predict answers 'will GitHub call this conflicted?'. The duplication that reddened main TWICE on 2026-09-17 is a merge that does NOT conflict and whose RESULT is corrupt, so predict returned `clean` for exactly the case that broke main, both times. predict already builds the merged worktree and threw it away unexamined; it now offers it to an `inspect` hook first, and predicted_register_integrity grades that tree for duplicate ids using check_register_ids.py's own REGISTERS and check_uniqueness -- IMPORTED, never re-derived, with a test asserting IDENTITY rather than equality. THREE MEASURED FACTS, and the class needs all three. (1) IT IS NOT UNION, which is how the row was filed: a named-but-undefined driver falls back to git's ordinary three-way text merge. One fixture, two arms -- separated insertions merge clean and duplicate, ADJACENT ones CONFLICT -- and union never conflicts by construction, so the second arm is impossible under it. That also explains why the class is INTERMITTENT rather than constant. (2) 'No local check can catch it', the row's own words, is REFUTED: an un-armed clone reproduces the squash byte-identically, 9,118,392 bytes on the real #12374 incident. (3) WHAT DEFEATED CI WAS THE BASE MOVING -- #12374's guards finished 09:11:38Z against 5979618dc (1598 rows, 0 dupes, guard exit 0, CORRECTLY green) and the squash ran 09:29:15Z against 07f1417e6, which did not exist until 09:28:07Z. So no PR-time check closes this by binding its own base, whatever base it binds. AND THE ROW'S PRESCRIBED REMEDY IS INERT FOR THE POPULATION THAT CAUSES IT: over the COMPLETE population of all 29 PR-merge commits on main inside the window guards.yml's 100-run push page covers, a user-credential merge has a push run 5 of 5 and a GITHUB_TOKEN merge 0 of 24 -- perfect separation, zero exceptions -- so the PRs that land with no post-merge check are exactly the auto-merged ones. [!] The credential is the discriminator, NOT whether a human clicked: the MCP authenticates as the user account, so what is established is 'not GITHUB_TOKEN'. CONTROLS: 18 pytest cases and 86 preflight self-test cases (73 -> 86). EIGHT defects planted, EIGHT caught, NONE absorbed. [!] Six were initially caught only by pytest, which pytest-run short-circuits -- a control only the skippable job runs can be skipped -- so four pure-half cases were added to _self_test and re-planting confirms the two that matter most now redden there too. The real incident is a PERMANENT REGRESSION FIXTURE rather than a synthetic case, skipped on a shallow clone instead of silently passing. USED ON A REAL MERGE DECISION, UNPLANNED: #12402 sat green on all five checks and would not merge; one call returned github_mergeability FAIL (it had gone dirty as main moved) and predicted_register_integrity UNKNOWN, 'no named branch produced a mergeable tree to inspect -- this is not a pass'. After merging the base in, both read pass at 1608 rows / 0 duplicates, and that is what was pushed. [!] IT DOES NOT CLEAR THE ROW, and the criteria are sharpened to say so: this is a check the merge duty must be RUNNING at merge time, and nothing has yet been observed refusing a real merge with it -- the same gap #12393 records for the predictor it extends. It also does not close the post-merge hole. VERIFIED ON COMMITTED STATE: full guard set PASS 83 / FAIL 3, and TWO of those three were real findings of mine, now fixed and re-verified at EXIT 0 -- artifact-validity caught a TRUNCATED tracking id inside the module whose subject is not collapsing states (the fifth instance of that class in this repo today, written by an author actively describing it) plus a cross-PR dangling reference to a row that lives on #12402's branch and not on main (replaced with the PR number, which cannot dangle), and diagnostic-provenance caught sub-class C on the CLI's could-not-look line, which stated a verdict about registers without saying how many it read. The third is pr-landing-guard, which this record is the second push for. register-id-guard OK, claim-basis 0 findings, backlog round-trip byte-for-byte on all four registers, ruff clean. [!] A NEAR-MISS RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: my first ruff reading was 17,396 errors and main itself read 17,359, because the sandbox carried ruff 0.16.7 while requirements-dev.txt pins <0.16 PRECISELY because 0.16 expanded its default rule set. Acting on that delta would have meant 'fixing' 37 non-findings. With the pinned version: All checks passed.
